questions.question: The ratio of the number of boys to that of the girls in a school is 9 : 7. If the number of girls in the school is 189, then the number of boys in that school will be:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Boys** : **Girls** = 9 : 7

Given, 7 units (Girls) = 189

Value of 1 unit = 189 ÷ 7 = 27

Number of **Boys** = 9 units = 9 × 27 = 243

**∴ The correct answer is 243.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **Boys** to **Girls** = 9 : 7

Total number of **girls** = 189

**Formula Used:**

If the ratio of two quantities is a : b, and the value of one quantity is known, the other can be found using the **unitary method** or the **constant of proportionality** (x).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fda7ece4d54ec1821c8ed41429ddd06c43a85569e5f49bac1dca7ad8156f3910.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the number of **boys** in the school be 9x and **girls** be 7x.

⇒ According to the question, 7x = 189

⇒ x = 189 ÷ 7

⇒ x = 27

⇒ Now, number of **boys** = 9x

⇒ Number of **boys** = 9 × 27

⇒ Number of **boys** = 243

**∴ The correct answer is 243.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportion

A **ratio** is a comparison of two quantities of the same kind by division. If a/b = c/d, then a, b, c, d are in **proportion**.

Scaling of Ratios

Multiplying or dividing both terms of a **ratio** by the same non-zero number does not change the ratio (a : b = am : bm).

Mean and Extreme Proportional

In the proportion a : b :: c : d, the **product of extremes** (a × d) is always equal to the **product of means** (b × c).</p

questions.question: A convex mirror created a highly diminished, point-sized virtual image, then the position of the image is:

options.text: in front of the mirror at the centre of curvature C
behind the mirror at the focus F
behind the mirror at the centre of curvature C
in front of the mirror at the focus F

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**behind the mirror at the focus F**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image of an object placed in front of it.
 
• When an object is placed at an infinite distance from a convex mirror, the image formed is highly diminished and point-sized.
 
• The position of this highly diminished, virtual image is located at the focal point (F) of the convex mirror, behind the mirror.
 
• This property of convex mirrors makes them suitable for use as rearview mirrors in vehicles, as they provide a wider field of view.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Focal Point (F):** The point at which parallel rays of light either converge or appear to diverge after reflecting off the mirror.
 
• **Centre of Curvature (C):** The center of the sphere from which the mirror segment is cut. For convex mirrors, it lies behind the mirror.
 
• **Principal Axis:** The line passing through the center of curvature and the midpoint of the mirror.
 
• **Ray Diagrams for Convex Mirrors:** Useful for understanding the image formation, showing the path of rays and how they reflect to form images.
 
• **Applications of Convex Mirrors:** Used in vehicle rearview mirrors, security mirrors, and in places requiring a wide-angle view.

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 5, and their LCM is 1600. The HCF of the numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **HCF** of the numbers be x.

The numbers in the ratio 1 : 2 : 5 are x, 2x, and 5x.

The **LCM** of 1, 2, and 5 is 10. Thus, LCM of the numbers is 10 × x = 10x.

Given 10x = 1600 ⇒ x = 160.

**∴ The correct answer is 160.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of three numbers = 1 : 2 : 5, and their **LCM** = 1600.

**Formula Used:** For numbers ax, bx, and cx where x is the **HCF**, their LCM is x × LCM(a, b, c).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b613b90c105006e87b4f48602723a8a028b886811f2b4133e80b39deb8811350.png] 

Let the common multiplier be x, which also represents the **HCF** of the three numbers.

⇒ First number = 1x

⇒ Second number = 2x

⇒ Third number = 5x

⇒ LCM of (1x, 2x, 5x) = x × LCM(1, 2, 5)

⇒ LCM = x × 10 = 10x

⇒ 10x = 1600

⇒ x = 160

∴ The **HCF** of the numbers is 160.

**∴ The correct answer is 160.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and HCF Relationship

For any set of numbers, their HCF is always a factor of their LCM. The ratios of the numbers, when multiplied by their HCF, yield the original numbers.

Product of Two Numbers Formula

For any two numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: A × B = HCF × LCM.</p

questions.question: Plasma membrane is made up of ______

The correct answer is __**Both proteins and lipids**__.

__
 
• The plasma membrane is primarily composed of a bilayer of lipids, mainly phospholipids, with embedded proteins.
 
• Phospholipids form the fundamental structure, creating a semi-permeable membrane.
 
• Proteins in the plasma membrane serve various functions including transport, signal transduction, and acting as enzymes.
 
• The fluid mosaic model describes the plasma membrane as a dynamic arrangement of phospholipids and proteins.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phospholipids**:

 
 
• Composed of a hydrophilic (water-attracting) "head" and two hydrophobic (water-repelling) "tails".
 
• They arrange themselves into a bilayer in aqueous environments, with heads facing outward and tails inward.
 
 
 
• **Integral Proteins**:
 
 
• Span the entire membrane and are involved in transport and communication across the membrane.
 
 
 
• **Peripheral Proteins**:
 
 
• Located on the surface of the membrane and play a role in cell signaling and maintaining the cell's shape.
 
 
 
• **Cholesterol**:
 
 
• Present within the lipid bilayer, it helps to stabilize the fluidity of the membrane.
 
 
 
• **Glycoproteins and Glycolipids**:
 
 
• Carbohydrate chains attached to proteins and lipids, involved in cell recognition and signaling.

questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself on compound interest in 15 years. In what duration will it become 8 times of itself, considering annual compounding?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In **Compound Interest**, if a sum becomes **n** times in **T** years, it becomes **nx** times in **x × T** years.

Given: **n = 2** times in **T = 15** years.

We need **8** times, which is **2³** times.

Here, **x = 3**. Therefore, **Required Time = 3 × 15 = 45 years**.

**∴ The correct answer is 45 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0b89f1d30f26f3e203e84ca4802e7ee9a027bd455f6b872c059ef07f2f25cd8.png] 

**Given:** Sum becomes **2 times** in 15 years.

**Formula:** Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)t

⇒ 2P = P(1 + r/100)¹⁵

⇒ 2 = (1 + r/100)¹⁵ --- (Equation 1)

To find time (t) for **8 times** the sum:

⇒ 8P = P(1 + r/100)t

⇒ 8 = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ 2³ = (1 + r/100)t

Substituting the value of 2 from Equation 1:

⇒ [(1 + r/100)¹⁵]³ = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ (1 + r/100)⁴⁵ = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ t = **45 years**

**∴ The correct answer is 45 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The formula for annual compounding is A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ, where A is the amount, P is the principal, r is the rate, and n is the time in years.

Rule of doubling (CI)

In CI, the time taken for a sum to grow from 1 to 2, 2 to 4, 4 to 8, and so on, remains constant for a fixed interest rate.

SI vs CI growth

Simple interest grows **linearly** (constant addition), whereas Compound Interest grows **exponentially** (constant multiplication).</p

questions.question: Variation is useful for the survival of species over time. These variations occur due to errors in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**DNA copying**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Variations are crucial for the survival and evolution of species, providing a way for organisms to adapt to changing environments.
 
• These variations occur due to errors in the DNA copying process during cell division.
 
• Such errors, known as mutations, can introduce new traits in organisms which may enhance their survival and reproduction.
 
• While some mutations can be harmful, others can be beneficial and contribute to the genetic diversity of a population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **DNA Replication:**

 
 
• DNA replication is the process by which a DNA molecule makes a copy of itself during cell division.
 
• It ensures that each new cell receives an exact copy of the organism's genetic material.
 
• The process involves enzymes like DNA polymerase, which helps in adding nucleotides to the growing DNA strand.
 
 
 
• **Mutation:**
 
 
• A mutation is a change in the DNA sequence that can lead to variations in the genetic code.
 
• Mutations can occur spontaneously or be induced by external factors such as radiation and chemicals.
 
• They play a critical role in evolution by introducing new genetic variations.
 
 
 
• **Genetic Variation:**
 
 
• Genetic variation refers to the differences in DNA sequences among individuals within a population.
 
• It is essential for natural selection, as it provides the raw material for evolutionary change.
 
• High genetic variation within a population increases its ability to adapt to environmental changes.
 
 
 
• **Natural Selection:**
 
 
• Natural selection is the process by which organisms with advantageous traits are more likely to survive and reproduce.
 
• Over time, these advantageous traits become more common within the population.
 
• Natural selection drives the evolution of species by favoring traits that enhance survival and reproductive success.

questions.question: If 85% of a number is added to 24, then the result is the same number. 75% of the same number is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let the **number** be 100%.

Given: 85% + 24 = 100% ⇒ 15% = 24.

We need to find 75% of the number.

If 15% → 24, then 75% → 24 × (75 ÷ 15) = 24 × 5 = 120.

**∴ The correct answer is 120.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8469b54b8023427406572f8b942c0f65710a63cd7e38962eb86ee248258decfb.png] 

**Given:** 85% of a number + 24 = the number itself.

**Formula:** Value = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Total Number

⇒ Let the number be x.

⇒ 0.85x + 24 = x

⇒ x − 0.85x = 24

⇒ 0.15x = 24

⇒ x = 24 ÷ 0.15 = 160

⇒ 75% of 160 = 0.75 × 160

⇒ 75% of 160 = 120

**∴ The correct answer is 120.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

Percentage change = (Difference ÷ Original Value) × 100. This is useful for finding the gap between 85% and 100%.

Fraction Equivalent

Converting percentages to fractions can simplify calculations: 75% = 3/4 and 15% = 3/20.

Base Change Rule

If 15% of a number is added to make it 100%, the added value is always equal to the remaining percentage of that total base.</p

questions.question: Which of the following is used in the oxidation of alcohol into carboxylic acid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alkaline potassium permanganate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Alkaline potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) is a strong oxidizing agent used to convert primary alcohols into carboxylic acids.
 
• The oxidation process involves the formation of an aldehyde intermediate, which further oxidizes to form the carboxylic acid.
 
• This reagent is often used in organic chemistry due to its effectiveness and relatively straightforward reaction mechanism.
 
• Alkaline potassium permanganate is preferred in many laboratory and industrial applications because of its ability to provide high yields of the desired carboxylic acid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxidation of Alcohols**:

 
 
• Primary alcohols are oxidized to aldehydes and further to carboxylic acids.
 
• Secondary alcohols are oxidized to ketones, which generally do not undergo further oxidation under mild conditions.
 
• Tertiary alcohols are resistant to oxidation due to the absence of hydrogen atoms on the carbon bearing the hydroxyl group.
 
 
 
• **Potassium Permanganate (KMnO₄)**:
 
 
• It is a dark purple, crystalline compound that is highly soluble in water.
 
• In its alkaline form, KMnO₄ provides an effective oxidizing environment.
 
• It is widely used for its disinfectant and oxidizing properties in various chemical reactions.
 
 
 
• **Reaction Mechanism**:
 
 
• The oxidation of a primary alcohol to a carboxylic acid involves the removal of hydrogen atoms and the addition of oxygen atoms.
 
• This process typically involves intermediate steps, including the formation of an aldehyde.
 
• The reaction is typically carried out under controlled conditions to ensure complete oxidation.
 
 
 
• **Applications**:
 
 
• Oxidation reactions are crucial in the synthesis of various organic compounds.
 
• They are used in the pharmaceutical industry for the production of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs).
 
• Such reactions are also important in the production of fine chemicals and in environmental chemistry for pollutant degradation.

questions.question: If the radius of a sphere is halved, then the new volume will become ______ the original volume.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **volume** of a sphere is proportional to the **cube** of its **radius** (V ∝ r³).

If the radius becomes **1/2** of its original value, the volume change ratio = (1/2)³.

Calculation: (1/2) × (1/2) × (1/2) = 1/8.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/8 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Original radius = r, New radius = r/2

**Formula Used:** Volume of a Sphere (V) = (4/3)πr³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0054b41725528f2b0fc7d835bcd8ead909eab64f995672f9e306bbe86fd1bd60.png] 

⇒ Original Volume (V₁) = (4/3) × π × r³

⇒ New Volume (V₂) = (4/3) × π × (r/2)³

⇒ V₂ = (4/3) × π × (r³ / 8)

⇒ V₂ = (1/8) × [(4/3) × π × r³]

⇒ V₂ = (1/8) × V₁

**∴ The correct answer is 1/8 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Surface Area of a Sphere

The surface area is given by 4πr². If the radius is halved, the surface area becomes (1/2)² = 1/4 of the original.

Volume of a Hemisphere

A hemisphere is half of a sphere, and its volume is given by (2/3)πr³.

Ratio of Volumes

For any similar 3D shapes, the ratio of their volumes is the cube of the ratio of their corresponding linear dimensions (Side₁/Side₂)³.</p

questions.question: Amphibians have a _______ chambered heart.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Amphibians, such as frogs and salamanders, have a three-chambered heart.
 
• The heart consists of two atria and one ventricle.
 
• The three-chambered heart allows for some separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.
 
• This structure is an evolutionary adaptation suited to their dual life in water and on land.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxygenation Process:**

 
 
• In amphibians, the heart pumps both oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, which partially mixes in the single ventricle.
 
• This mixed blood is then sent to the lungs and skin for oxygenation and to the rest of the body.
 
 
 
• **Circulatory System:**
 
 
• Amphibians have a double circulatory system, with separate pulmonary and systemic circuits.
 
• This system is more efficient than a single circulatory system but less efficient than a four-chambered heart.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Vertebrates:**
 
 
• Fish have a two-chambered heart (one atrium and one ventricle).
 
• Birds and mammals have a four-chambered heart (two atria and two ventricles), which allows for complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.
 
 
 
• **Evolutionary Significance:**
 
 
• The three-chambered heart of amphibians represents an intermediate stage in the evolution of the more complex hearts of higher vertebrates.
 
• This adaptation is essential for amphibians' survival in both aquatic and terrestrial environments.

• These are series of compounds with the same functional group and similar chemical properties, where each successive member differs by a CH2 unit.
 
• Examples include the alkane series (CnH2n+2), alkene series (CnH2n), and alcohol series (CnH2n+1OH).

• Phenol (C6H5OH) is an aromatic compound where a hydroxyl group (-OH) is bonded to a benzene ring.

• **Alcohols:**

• Common functional groups include hydroxyl (-OH), carboxyl (-COOH), and amino (-NH2).

questions.question: The twinkling of stars is due to _______

options.text: the atmospheric reflection of light from the stars
the atmospheric refraction of light from the star
the interference of light from a star and moon
the interference of light from different stars

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the atmospheric refraction of light from the star**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The twinkling of stars is primarily caused by the atmospheric refraction of light as it passes through different layers of Earth's atmosphere.
 
• As the light from a star travels through the Earth's atmosphere, it constantly changes direction due to the varying density and temperature of the atmospheric layers.
 
• This continuous change in direction causes the star's light to appear as if it is twinkling when observed from the Earth's surface.
 
• The phenomenon is more pronounced for stars closer to the horizon because their light passes through a greater thickness of the Earth's atmosphere.
 
• Planets do not twinkle as much as stars because they have a larger apparent size, which averages out the variations in light due to atmospheric refraction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atmospheric Refraction:**

 
 
• Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another, caused by a change in the speed of light in different media.
 
• In the context of stars, atmospheric refraction is the bending of starlight as it passes through the Earth's atmosphere, which has varying densities and temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Scintillation:**
 
 
• Scintillation refers to the rapid variations in the brightness and color of stars caused by atmospheric turbulence. It is often used synonymously with "twinkling."
 
 
 
• **Light Pollution:**
 
 
• Light pollution from urban areas can also affect the visibility of stars, making the twinkling effect less noticeable in cities compared to rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Seeing Conditions:**
 
 
• "Seeing" refers to the steadiness of the Earth's atmosphere. Poor seeing conditions, caused by atmospheric turbulence, can enhance the twinkling effect of stars.

questions.question: The present age of a teacher is 1(1)/(2) times the sum of the present ages of his two students. Six years hence, the ratio of his age to the sum of the ages of both the students will be 6 : 5. The present age of the teacher is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Present Ratio (Teacher : Sum of Students) = 1.5 : 1 ⇒ 3 : 2

Ratio after 6 years = 6 : 5

Since there are 2 students, the sum of their ages increases by 6 × 2 = 12 years, while the teacher's age increases by 6 years.

Let present ages be 3x and 2x. ⇒ (3x + 6) / (2x + 12) = 6 / 5

⇒ 15x + 30 = 12x + 72 ⇒ 3x = 42 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4213033f70ec0d14ecedeb0951b14411e6be94408614c77a12930d9fcbe36fbc.png] 

**Given:**

Let the **present sum of ages** of the two students be **S**.

The **present age** of the teacher **T = 1.5S** = (3/2)S.

**Calculations:**

⇒ T / S = 3 / 2 ⇒ T = 3x and S = 2x.

⇒ After 6 years, Teacher age = T + 6 = 3x + 6.

⇒ After 6 years, Sum of students age = S + (6 × 2) = 2x + 12 (since there are two students).

⇒ Given ratio after 6 years: (3x + 6) / (2x + 12) = 6 / 5

⇒ 5 × (3x + 6) = 6 × (2x + 12)

⇒ 15x + 30 = 12x + 72

⇒ 3x = 42

⇒ Teacher present age T = 3x = 42 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ages of Multiple Persons

When calculating the sum of ages for **n** people after **t** years, always add **n × t** to the initial sum.

Ratio and Proportion in Ages

If the ratio of ages is given as a:b, it is often easiest to assume the values as ax and bx to form linear equations based on time shifts.</p

questions.question: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 6 and 1824, respectively. If one number is 96, then the other number is:

questions.question: The highest common factor of any two distinct prime numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
**Prime numbers** have only two factors: 1 and themselves.

For any two **distinct prime numbers**, the only common divisor they share is 1.

Therefore, their **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** is always 1.
**∴ The correct answer is 1.**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Two distinct prime numbers, let them be p and q.

**Formula Used:** HCF is the largest positive integer that divides each of the integers.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8fe63cf076058b263c27dddccb579c7da7465ad5f19a6874b8da603320dc330f.png] 
**Calculations:**

⇒ Let us assume two distinct prime numbers: 3 and 5.

⇒ Factors of 3 = 1, 3

⇒ Factors of 5 = 1, 5

⇒ Common Factor = 1

⇒ HCF(3, 5) = 1

⇒ This property holds true for any pair of distinct prime numbers.
**∴ The correct answer is 1.**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Coprime Numbers

Any two numbers whose HCF is 1 are called coprime numbers. Thus, any two distinct prime numbers are always coprime.

LCM of Prime Numbers

The Least Common Multiple (LCM) of any two distinct prime numbers p and q is always their product, i.e., p × q.

Lowest Prime Number

The number 2 is the smallest prime number and the only even prime number in existence.</p

questions.question: The sum of all the prime numbers between 51 and 100 is:
questions.solution:

Identify **prime numbers** in each decade from 51 to 100.

51 to 60: 53, 59 (Sum = 112)

61 to 70: 61, 67 (Sum = 128)

71 to 80: 71, 73, 79 (Sum = 223)

81 to 90: 83, 89 (Sum = 172)

91 to 100: 97 (Sum = 97)

Prime Numbers from 1 to 100

questions.question: The wickets taken by a bowler in 10 cricket matches are 2, 6, 4, 5, 0, 3, 1, 3, 2, 3. The median of the data is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the 10 data points in ascending order: 0, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 5, 6.

Since the number of observations (n) is 10 (even), the median is the average of the 5th and 6th terms.

The 5th term is 3 and the 6th term is 3.

Median = (3 + 3) ÷ 2 = 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Wickets taken in 10 matches: 2, 6, 4, 5, 0, 3, 1, 3, 2, 3.

**Formula Used:**

When the number of observations (n) is even:

Median = [(n/2)th term + (n/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6d880dfaaeeea127a57879b4affee779dc46256c6d8bcc5f2b8a7fcf81fd1042.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total number of matches (n) = 10

⇒ Arrange the data in ascending order: 0, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 5, 6

⇒ n/2 = 5th term = 3

⇒ n/2 + 1 = 6th term = 3

⇒ Median = (3 + 3) ÷ 2 = 6 ÷ 2 = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Median for Odd Number of Terms

If n is odd, the median is the value of the ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th term after arranging the data in ascending order.

Mode of Data

The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set. For this dataset, the mode is 3 as it appears three times.

Empirical Relationship

The relationship between mean, median, and mode is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.</p

questions.question: Ram applied the brakes to his cycle and an acceleration of 2 m s⁻² is produced in the opposite direction to the motion. If the cycle takes 10 s to stop after the application of brakes, calculate the distance it travels during this time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The initial velocity (u) of the cycle is not given but can be calculated since the final velocity (v) is 0 m/s (cycle stops).
 
• The acceleration (a) is given as -2 m/s² (negative sign indicates deceleration).
 
• The time (t) taken to stop the cycle is 10 seconds.
 
• Using the first equation of motion: v = u + at, we get 0 = u - 2 * 10, therefore u = 20 m/s.
 
• Using the second equation of motion: s = ut + 0.5 * a * t², we get s = 20 * 10 + 0.5 * (-2) * 10² = 200 - 100 = 100 meters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Equations of Motion:**

 
 
• The three equations of motion are: v = u + at, s = ut + 0.5 * a * t², and v² = u² + 2as.
 
• These equations are used to calculate final velocity, displacement, and final velocity squared respectively.
 
 
 
• **Deceleration:**
 
 
• Deceleration refers to a decrease in speed or velocity.
 
• It is represented by a negative acceleration in physics equations.
 
 
 
• **Stopping Distance:**
 
 
• The stopping distance is the distance a vehicle travels while coming to a complete stop.
 
• It is affected by the initial speed, the rate of deceleration, and the reaction time of the driver.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• Understanding motion and deceleration is crucial in designing safe braking systems for vehicles.
 
• It helps in accident reconstruction and traffic safety analysis.

questions.question: In males if the ______ is surgically cut, sperm transfer will be prevented.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**vas deferens**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The vas deferens is a long, muscular tube that transports mature sperm from the epididymis to the urethra in preparation for ejaculation.
 
• Surgical cutting or sealing of the vas deferens is known as a vasectomy, which is a common form of male sterilization.
 
• During a vasectomy, the vas deferens is either cut and sealed or tied, preventing sperm from mixing with the semen that is ejaculated from the penis.
 
• The procedure is highly effective at preventing pregnancy, with a success rate of over 99%.
 
• A vasectomy does not affect the production of male hormones, sexual function, or the ability to ejaculate semen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prostate Gland**

 
 
• The prostate gland produces fluid that nourishes and transports sperm during ejaculation.
 
• It is located just below the bladder and surrounds the urethra.
 
• Enlargement of the prostate gland can lead to urinary problems in older men.
 
 
 
• **Fallopian Tube**
 
 
• The fallopian tubes are part of the female reproductive system.
 
• They transport eggs from the ovaries to the uterus.
 
• Fertilization of the egg by sperm typically occurs in the fallopian tubes.
 
 
 
• **Seminal Vesicles**
 
 
• The seminal vesicles are glands that secrete a fluid rich in sugar that provides energy for sperm.
 
• They contribute approximately 60% of the fluid in semen.
 
• The fluid from the seminal vesicles mixes with sperm to form semen.

questions.question: A man has invested Rs. 75,000 at a rate of 7(1)/(2)\% per annum simple interest for 6 years. Find the amount that he will receive after 6 years.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **Simple Interest** % for 6 years = Rate × Time = 7.5% × 6 = 45%.

**Amount** % = 100% (Principal) + 45% (Interest) = 145%.

**Total Amount** = 145% of ₹75,000 = 1.45 × 75,000 = ₹1,08,750.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,08,750.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Principal (P)** = ₹75,000, **Rate (R)** = 7.5% per annum, **Time (T)** = 6 years.

**Formula Used:** Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100; Amount (A) = P + SI

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fab2219914058d000a765ea265d562bc2bc37ec8d3bf4f27782ce157907a9408.png] 

⇒ SI = (75000 × 7.5 × 6) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 750 × 45

⇒ SI = ₹33,750

⇒ Amount = Principal + SI = 75,000 + 33,750

⇒ Amount = ₹1,08,750

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,08,750.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Properties

Simple Interest remains constant for every year if the principal and rate are unchanged. SI = P × R × T ÷ 100.

Amount Calculation

The total money returned after the tenure is called Amount. A = P(1 + RT/100).

Effective Rate of Interest

In Simple Interest, the effective rate for 't' years is simply (R × t)%. For Compound Interest, it follows successive percentage change.

questions.question: There are two sections A and B of a class, consisting of 36 and 44 students, respectively. If the average weight of students of section A is 40 kg and that of section B is 35 kg, find the average weight of the whole class.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of students in **Section A** and **Section B** = 36 : 44 = 9 : 11.

Assume **weighted average** using deviation from 35 kg: [9 × (40 − 35) + 11 × (35 − 35)] ÷ (9 + 11).

Net deviation = (9 × 5) ÷ 20 = 45 ÷ 20 = 2.25 kg.

Actual Average = 35 + 2.25 = 37.25 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 37.25 kg.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/39b26edcc5d6a88443cc11891f76f53e4ba629ced92adbc7c53788e775aaf0f8.png] 

**Given:**

Students in **Section A** (n₁) = 36, Average (A₁) = 40 kg

Students in **Section B** (n₂) = 44, Average (A₂) = 35 kg

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of **Section A** = 36 × 40 = 1440 kg

⇒ Total weight of **Section B** = 44 × 35 = 1540 kg

⇒ Total weight of class = 1440 + 1540 = 2980 kg

⇒ Total number of students = 36 + 44 = 80

⇒ Average weight of whole class = 2980 ÷ 80

⇒ Average weight = 37.25 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 37.25 kg.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

It is used when groups have different sizes. Formula: W = (Σ nᵢwᵢ) ÷ Σ nᵢ.

Deviation Method

New Average = Assumed Average + (Total Deviation ÷ Total Number). This simplifies large multiplications.

Alligation Rule

The ratio of quantities is inversely proportional to the difference between their averages and the mean average.</p

questions.question: Suresh spends 30% of his income on petrol, (1)/(4) of the remaining income on house rent, and the balance on food. If he spends ₹300 on petrol, then what is his expenditure on house rent?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Expenditure on **petrol** = 30% of **Income** = ₹300.

⇒ 100% **Income** = (300 ÷ 30) × 100 = ₹1,000.

**Remaining income** after petrol = ₹1,000 − ₹300 = ₹700.

**House rent** = 1/4 of **Remaining income** = 700 ÷ 4 = ₹175.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹175.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ (30/100) × X = 300

⇒ X = (300 × 100) ÷ 30 = ₹1,000

⇒ **Remaining income** = Total Income − Petrol expense

⇒ **Remaining income** = 1000 − 300 = ₹700

⇒ **House rent** = (1/4) × 700

A fraction of 1/4 is equivalent to 25%. Calculating 1/4 of a value is the same as taking 25% of it.

Base Value Identification

Always identify if a percentage is applied to the **total income** or the **remaining income** to avoid calculation errors.

questions.question: The most scattered colour of the sun light when it enters the earth’s atmosphere is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**blue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Blue light has the shortest wavelength (about 450-495 nanometers) among the visible spectrum, which makes it scatter more than other colors when it enters the Earth's atmosphere.
 
• The scattering of blue light by air molecules causes the sky to appear blue during the daytime, a phenomenon known as Rayleigh scattering.
 
• When sunlight passes through the atmosphere, shorter wavelengths of light (blue and violet) are scattered in all directions by the gases and particles in the air.
 
• The human eye is more sensitive to blue light than to violet light, which is why we see the sky as blue rather than violet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rayleigh Scattering:**

 
 
• Named after the British scientist Lord Rayleigh, this type of scattering occurs when the particles causing the scattering are smaller than the wavelength of the light.
 
• It is responsible for the blue color of the sky and the reddening of the sun at sunrise and sunset.
 
 
 
• **Visible Spectrum:**
 
 
• The visible spectrum is the portion of the electromagnetic spectrum that is visible to the human eye, ranging from approximately 380 to 750 nanometers.
 
• Colors in the visible spectrum include violet, blue, green, yellow, orange, and red.
 
 
 
• **Wavelength and Frequency:**
 
 
• Light waves are characterized by their wavelength (the distance between successive peaks) and frequency (the number of peaks passing a point per second).
 
• Shorter wavelengths correspond to higher frequencies and higher energy.
 
 
 
• **Mie Scattering:**
 
 
• This type of scattering occurs when the particles causing the scattering are about the same size as the wavelength of the light.
 
• Mie scattering is responsible for the white appearance of clouds, as it scatters all wavelengths of light equally.

options.text: Both solid state and liquid state

__
 
• The gaseous state is characterized by particles that are far apart and move freely, making gases highly compressible.
 
• Compressibility is a measure of the relative volume change of a fluid or solid as a response to a pressure change.
 
• Gases can be compressed into much smaller volumes compared to solids and liquids.
 
• Due to the large amount of empty space between gas particles, they can be squeezed together under pressure.
 
• Examples of highly compressible gases include air, carbon dioxide, and helium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Solids have a fixed shape and volume with particles closely packed in a regular pattern.
 
• They are incompressible due to the minimal space between particles.
 
• Examples include ice, iron, and wood.
 
 
 
• **Liquid State**
 
 
• Liquids have a fixed volume but take the shape of their container.
 
• They are slightly compressible because particles are close together but can move past each other.
 
• Examples include water, oil, and mercury.
 
 
 
• **Boyle's Law**
 
 
• It states that the pressure of a given mass of gas is inversely proportional to its volume at a constant temperature.
 
• This law explains the compressibility of gases.

• Compressed natural gas (CNG) is used as a fuel for vehicles.
 
• Compressed air is used in pneumatic tools and machinery.

questions.question: Rahul can do a piece of work in 20 days whereas Rohan can do the same work in 30 days. Both started the work together and worked for 6 days with full efficiency, and in the next 6 days with half of their efficiencies. In how many days will the remaining work be finished if both work with their full efficiencies for the remaining period?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Work (LCM of 20, 30) = 60 units. Efficiency: Rahul = 3, Rohan = 2.

Combined Full Efficiency = 3 + 2 = 5 units/day; Half Efficiency = 2.5 units/day.

Work done in first 6 days (Full) = 6 × 5 = 30 units.

Work done in next 6 days (Half) = 6 × 2.5 = 15 units.

Remaining Work = 60 − (30 + 15) = 15 units.

Remaining Days = 15 ÷ 5 = 3 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **Rahul** = 20 days

Time taken by **Rohan** = 30 days

Total work = LCM(20, 30) = 60 units

 **Efficiency**

 20

 30

⇒ Total combined efficiency (Full) = 3 + 2 = 5 units/day

⇒ Total combined efficiency (Half) = 5 ÷ 2 = 2.5 units/day

⇒ Work completed in 1st 6 days = 6 × 5 = 30 units

⇒ Work completed in 2ⁿd 6 days = 6 × 2.5 = 15 units

⇒ Total work done = 30 + 15 = 45 units

⇒ Remaining work = 60 − 45 = 15 units

⇒ Time taken to finish remaining work (Full efficiency) = 15 ÷ 5 = 3 days

Simplify the following expression:

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Put **θ = 90°** in the given expression.

⇒ [sin 90° / (1 + cos 90°)] + [(1 + cos 90°) / sin 90°]

⇒ [1 / (1 + 0)] + [(1 + 0) / 1] = 1 + 1 = **2**.

Check options for θ = 90°: (2) 2 cosec 90° = 2 × 1 = **2**.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 cosec θ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** [sin θ / (1 + cos θ)] + [(1 + cos θ) / sin θ]

**Formula Used:** sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; cosec θ = 1 / sin θ

⇒ Take **LCM** of denominators: sin θ (1 + cos θ)

⇒ [sin²θ + (1 + cos θ)²] / [sin θ (1 + cos θ)]

⇒ [sin²θ + 1 + cos²θ + 2 cos θ] / [sin θ (1 + cos θ)]

⇒ [(sin²θ + cos²θ) + 1 + 2 cos θ] / [sin θ (1 + cos θ)]

⇒ [1 + 1 + 2 cos θ] / [sin θ (1 + cos θ)]

⇒ [2 + 2 cos θ] / [sin θ (1 + cos θ)]

⇒ 2(1 + cos θ) / [sin θ (1 + cos θ)]

⇒ 2 / sin θ = **2 cosec θ**

**∴ The correct answer is 2 cosec θ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities include **sin²θ + cos²θ = 1**, **1 + tan²θ = sec²θ**, and **1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ**.

Reciprocal Relations

The function **cosec θ** is the reciprocal of **sin θ**, and **sec θ** is the reciprocal of **cos θ**.</p

questions.question: What is the unit of universal gravitational constant (G)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**N m² kg⁻²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The universal gravitational constant (**G**) appears in Newton's law of gravitation, which describes the gravitational force between two masses.
 
• The correct SI unit of **G** is N m² kg⁻²__, where:
 __
 
• N stands for Newton (unit of force).
 
• m² stands for square meters (unit of distance squared).
 
• kg⁻² represents the inverse square of mass in kilograms.
 
 
 
• **G** is a proportionality constant that quantifies the strength of the gravitational force between two objects.
 
• The value of **G** is approximately 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²__.
 
• The universal gravitational constant is the same throughout the universe and is independent of the nature of the medium between the objects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's Law of Gravitation:**

 
 
• It states that every particle in the universe attracts every other particle with a force directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
• The formula is: F = G (m₁m₂) / r²__, where *F* is the gravitational force, *G* is the gravitational constant, *m₁* and *m₂* are the masses, and *r* is the distance between their centers.
 
 
 
• **Dimensional Formula of G:** [G] = M⁻¹L³T⁻², where M stands for mass, L for length, and T for time.
 
• **Importance of G:** The value of **G** enables the calculation of gravitational forces in celestial mechanics, such as the orbits of planets, moons, and satellites.
 
• **Gravitational Force vs. Electromagnetic Force:**
 
 
• Gravitational force is much weaker compared to electromagnetic force but acts over long distances.
 
• It is always attractive, unlike electromagnetic force, which can be both attractive and repulsive.
 
 
 
• **Discovery:** The value of **G** was first determined experimentally by Henry Cavendish in 1798 using a torsion balance.

x + y = 20

xy = 84

Sum and Difference Relation

questions.question: If 1.6 : 0.6 :: 0.6 : x, find the value of x.

For a **continued proportion** a : b :: b : x, the third proportional is **x = b² ÷ a**.

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is √(a × b).

Fourth Proportional

Third Proportional

questions.question: Which of the following is a property of isomers in organic chemistry?

options.text: They have different molecular formulas but the same structural ar

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Isomers are compounds that have the **same molecular formula** but differ in the **arrangement of atoms** within the molecules.
 
• They exhibit **different physical and chemical properties** despite having the same molecular formula.
 
• Isomers can be broadly classified into two categories: **structural isomers** and **stereoisomers**.
 
• Structural isomers have different **connectivity** of atoms, whereas stereoisomers have the same connectivity but differ in the **spatial arrangement** of atoms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structural Isomers**:

• Examples include chain isomers, positional isomers, and functional isomers.
 
 
 
• **Stereoisomers**:

• They can be further divided into enantiomers and diastereomers.
 
 
 
• **Enantiomers**:
 
 
• A type of stereoisomer where the molecules are non-superimposable mirror images of each other.
 
• They have identical physical properties except for their interaction with plane-polarized light and reactions with chiral environments.
 
 
 
• **Diastereomers**:
 
 
• Stereoisomers that are not mirror images of each other.
 
• They have different physical properties and reactivity.

questions.question: The sum of the present ages of Sarala and Kishore is 26 years. If 3 years ago, Kishore was (3)/(2) times as old as Sarala, then the present age of Sarala is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of ages 3 years ago = 26 − (2 × 3) = 20 years.

Ratio of **Kishore** to **Sarala** 3 years ago = 3 : 2.

Total ratio parts = 3 + 2 = 5 units → 20 years ⇒ 1 unit = 4 years.

**Sarala** age 3 years ago = 2 units = 2 × 4 = 8 years.

Present age of **Sarala** = 8 + 3 = 11 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ee398718d71361cec6ccc338883106042da84dfd015069634b2a62687256de31.png] 

**Given:** Sum of present ages = 26 years. Ratio (K:S) 3 years ago = 3 : 2.

⇒ Let **Sarala** present age be x and **Kishore** present age be y.

⇒ x + y = 26

⇒ 3 years ago: (y − 3) = 3/2 × (x − 3)

⇒ 2y − 6 = 3x − 9 ⇒ 3x − 2y = 3

⇒ From first eq, y = 26 − x. Substitute: 3x − 2(26 − x) = 3

⇒ 3x − 52 + 2x = 3 ⇒ 5x = 55

⇒ x = 11 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Age Ratio Shift

When moving 'n' years back in time for two people, the sum of their ages decreases by 2n.

Constant Difference

The difference between the ages of two persons remains constant throughout their lives, regardless of the years passed.</p

questions.question: If the magnification of any mirror is +2.3, which type of mirror is it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Concave mirror**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A concave mirror can produce a magnification greater than one, indicating that the image size is larger than the object size.
 
• Positive magnification in concave mirrors means the image is virtual and erect.
 
• Concave mirrors are often used in applications like shaving mirrors, makeup mirrors, and telescopes to provide a magnified view.
 
• Concave mirrors can form both real and virtual images, depending on the object's position relative to the mirror's focal point.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Focal Point:**

 
 
• The focal point of a concave mirror is the point where parallel rays of light converge after reflecting from the mirror.
 
• The distance from the mirror to the focal point is called the focal length.
 
 
 
• **Real Image vs. Virtual Image:**
 
 
• Real images are formed when light rays actually converge at a point, and they can be projected on a screen.
 
• Virtual images, like those formed by a concave mirror with positive magnification, appear to converge but do not actually do so; they cannot be projected on a screen.
 
 
 
• **Mirror Equation:**
 
 
• The mirror equation relates the object distance (u), image distance (v), and the focal length (f) of the mirror: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u.
 
• This equation helps in calculating the positions and nature of the image formed by the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Concave Mirrors:**
 
 
• Concave mirrors are used in reflecting telescopes to gather and focus light from distant stars and planets.
 
• They are also used in vehicle headlights to focus light into a beam.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The pancreas is responsible for secreting the enzyme trypsin, which is essential for protein digestion.
 
• Trypsin is produced in the pancreas in an inactive form called trypsinogen, which is then activated in the small intestine.
 
• The activation of trypsinogen to trypsin is mediated by the enzyme enterokinase, found in the lining of the small intestine.
 
• Trypsin plays a crucial role in the breakdown of proteins into smaller peptides, facilitating their absorption in the intestine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pancreatic Enzymes:**

 
 
• The pancreas secretes several digestive enzymes, including amylase, lipase, and nucleases, in addition to trypsin.
 
• These enzymes collectively aid in the digestion of carbohydrates, fats, and nucleic acids.
 
 
 
• **Protein Digestion:**
 
 
• Protein digestion begins in the stomach with the enzyme pepsin and continues in the small intestine with trypsin and other proteases.
 
 
 
• **Exocrine and Endocrine Functions:**
 
 
• The pancreas has both exocrine functions (secreting digestive enzymes) and endocrine functions (producing hormones like insulin and glucagon).
 
 
 
• **Activation of Pancreatic Enzymes:**
 
 
• Pancreatic enzymes are secreted in an inactive form to prevent auto-digestion of the pancreas.
 
• These enzymes are activated in the small intestine by various mechanisms, ensuring their function only where needed.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are NOT correct?

(i) Resistance of a conductor is independent of temperature.

(ii) The more the voltage across a resistor, the more is the current flowing through it.

(iii) The S.I unit of resistance is ohm.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The resistance of a conductor is not independent of temperature. For most conductive materials, resistance increases with temperature.
 
• Ohm's Law states that the current flowing through a resistor is directly proportional to the voltage across it, provided the temperature remains constant.
 
• The S.I. unit of resistance is indeed the ohm (Ω).
 
• Statement (i) is incorrect because resistance generally changes with temperature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Temperature Coefficient of Resistance:**

 
 
• The temperature coefficient of resistance quantifies how the resistance of a material changes with temperature.
 
• For metals, the temperature coefficient is positive, meaning resistance increases with temperature.
 
• For semiconductors and insulators, the temperature coefficient is generally negative.
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• Ohm's Law is given by V = IR, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
 
• This law is fundamental in electrical and electronic engineering.
 
 
 
• **Units of Electrical Resistance:**
 
 
• The ohm (Ω) is the S.I. unit of electrical resistance.
 
• It is named after the German physicist Georg Simon Ohm.
 
 
 
• **Conductivity and Resistivity:**
 
 
• Conductivity is the reciprocal of resistivity and measures a material's ability to conduct an electric current.
 
• Resistivity is a material-specific property that quantifies how strongly a material opposes the flow of electric current.

questions.question: Conventionally, the germ-cell containing the stored food is called the:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This process involves the formation of a primary oocyte, which then undergoes meiosis to form a mature ovum.
 
 
 
• **Fertilization**:
 
 
• Fertilization occurs when a male gamete (sperm) fuses with a female gamete (ovum).
 
• This fusion results in the formation of a zygote, which eventually develops into an embryo.
 
 
 
• **Gametes**:
 
 
• Gametes are the reproductive cells that unite during sexual reproduction to form a new organism.
 
• Male gametes are known as sperm, while female gametes are known as ova (eggs).

questions.question: Out of the following, which is a unit used for measuring the amount of work done on a body:
questions.solution:

__
 
• The Joule (symbol: J) is the SI unit of work or energy.
 
• It is defined as the work done when a force of one newton displaces a mass by one meter in the direction of the force.
 
• 1 Joule is equivalent to 1 Newton meter (N·m) or 1 kg·m²/s².
 
• The Joule is named after the English physicist James Prescott Joule who studied the nature of heat and discovered its relationship to mechanical work.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton:** It is the SI unit of force, not work. One Newton is the force required to accelerate a one-kilogram mass by one meter per second squared.
 
• **Meter:** It is the SI unit of length. One meter is the distance traveled by light in a vacuum in 1/299,792,458 seconds.
 
• **Kilogram:** It is the SI unit of mass. One kilogram is defined by the fixed numerical value of the Planck constant.
 
• **Work:** In physics, work is defined as the product of force and displacement. It is a scalar quantity and its unit is Joule in the SI system.

questions.question:
Which of the following scientists made the following statement?

“All cells arise from preexisting cells.”
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rudolf Virchow**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rudolf Virchow** was a German physician, anthropologist, pathologist, prehistorian, biologist, writer, editor, and politician.
 
• He is known for his advancement of public health and his famous statement, **"Omnis cellula e cellula"** which translates to "All cells arise from preexisting cells".
 
• Virchow's work in cell theory laid the foundation for modern pathology.
 
• He made significant contributions to understanding diseases at the cellular level, thus being considered one of the founding figures of modern medicine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell Theory**:

 
 
• Originally proposed by Matthias Schleiden and Theodor Schwann in 1838-1839.
 
• It states that all living organisms are composed of cells, and cells are the basic unit of structure and function in organisms.
 
• Virchow added the third tenet that all cells arise from preexisting cells, completing the modern cell theory.
 
 
 
• **Pathology**:
 
 
• It is the study of the causes and effects of disease or injury.
 
• Virchow's research in pathology helped understand that diseases could be traced to specific cell abnormalities.
 
 
 
• **Public Health**:
 
 
• Virchow was a pioneer in advocating for public health reforms.
 
• He worked on improving sanitation and hygiene to prevent the spread of diseases.
 
 
 
• **Microscopic Pathology**:
 
 
• Virchow's use of the microscope to study tissues and cells revolutionized the field of pathology.
 
• This approach allowed for the detailed study of disease processes at the cellular level.

questions.question: Which of the following cell organelles have their own DNA and ribosomes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4) Mitochondria**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mitochondria** are known as the powerhouse of the cell, generating most of the cell's supply of ATP, used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• Mitochondria have their own **circular DNA** (mtDNA), which is distinct from the cell's nuclear DNA.
 
• The presence of their own **ribosomes** allows mitochondria to synthesize some of their own proteins.
 
• Mitochondrial DNA is inherited maternally, meaning it is passed down from mother to offspring.
 
• They are involved in a range of other processes, including cell signaling, cellular differentiation, and the control of the cell cycle and cell growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Endosymbiotic Theory**:

 
 
• This theory suggests that mitochondria were once free-living prokaryotic organisms that were engulfed by ancestral eukaryotic cells.
 
• The symbiotic relationship provided the host cell with additional energy, while the engulfed organism received protection and a stable environment.
 
 
 
• **Chloroplasts**:
 
 
• Chloroplasts, found in plant cells and some algae, also contain their own DNA and ribosomes.
 
• Like mitochondria, chloroplasts are thought to have originated from endosymbiotic cyanobacteria.
 
 
 
• **Ribosomes**:
 
 
• Ribosomes are the molecular machines responsible for protein synthesis in cells.
 
• They read the information encoded in messenger RNA (mRNA) and translate it into a specific sequence of amino acids to form a protein.
 
 
 
• **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)**:
 
 
• ATP is the primary energy carrier in all living organisms on earth.
 
• It captures chemical energy obtained from the breakdown of food molecules and releases it to fuel other cellular processes.

questions.question: The marked price of an item was Rs. 2,000, but the shopkeeper offered successive discounts of 20% and 15% on its sale. How much did he finally sell the item for?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net discount % = a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)

Net discount = 20 + 15 − (20 × 15 ÷ 100) = 35 − 3 = 32%

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 − Net Discount%) ÷ 100

SP = 2000 × (100 − 32) ÷ 100 = 2000 × 68 ÷ 100 = 20 × 68 = 1360

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1360.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Marked Price (MP)** = Rs. 2000, **First Discount (d₁)** = 20%, **Second Discount (d₂)** = 15%.

**Formulas:** SP = MP × (100 − d₁)/100 × (100 − d₂)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/215c4cd7717cfca89c2ad7acb67c8aecd93a1c55ec84ac3730ce71194cd1868c.png] 

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 2000 × (80/100) = Rs. 1600

⇒ Price after 2ⁿd discount (Final SP) = 1600 × (85/100)

⇒ Final SP = 16 × 85 = Rs. 1360

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1360.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two or more discounts are applied one after another on the reduced price, they are called **successive discounts**. The total effective discount is always less than the sum of individual discount percentages.

Marked Price & Selling Price

**Marked Price (MP)** is the price printed on the label. **Selling Price (SP)** is the actual price after subtracting the **Discount** from the MP. SP = MP − Discount.</p

questions.question: Identify the nature of the functional group present in butanal.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aldehydes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Butanal is an organic compound with the chemical formula C₄H₈O.
 
• It belongs to the class of compounds known as aldehydes, characterized by the presence of a carbonyl group (C=O) attached to a hydrogen atom.
 
• The IUPAC name for butanal is butanal, but it is also known as butyraldehyde.
 
• The carbonyl group in butanal is located at the terminal carbon, making it an aldehyde rather than a ketone, which has the carbonyl group at a non-terminal carbon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Functional Groups:**

 
 
• A functional group is a specific group of atoms within a molecule that is responsible for the characteristic chemical reactions of that molecule.
 
• In organic chemistry, functional groups include alcohols, aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids, and more.
 
 
 
• **Aldehydes:**
 
 
• Aldehydes are organic compounds containing the functional group -CHO.
 
• They are typically named by replacing the -e at the end of the parent alkane name with -al (e.g., butane to butanal).
 
• Aldehydes are commonly found in fragrances and flavorings.
 
 
 
• **Ketones:**
 
 
• Ketones are organic compounds with the carbonyl group (C=O) bonded to two carbon atoms.
 
• They are named by replacing the -e at the end of the parent alkane name with -one (e.g., butane to butanone).
 
• Ketones are commonly used as solvents and in the chemical synthesis of other compounds.
 
 
 
• **Alcohols:**
 
 
• Alcohols are organic compounds containing the functional group -OH (hydroxyl group).
 
• They are named by replacing the -e at the end of the parent alkane name with -ol (e.g., butane to butanol).
 
• Alcohols are widely used in beverages, antiseptics, and fuels.

questions.question: Where does the oxygen-rich blood from the lungs come into the heart?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the left atrium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Oxygen-rich blood from the lungs enters the heart through the left atrium.
 
• The left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the pulmonary veins, which carry blood from the lungs.
 
• Once filled, the left atrium contracts, pushing blood into the left ventricle.
 
• The left ventricle then pumps the oxygenated blood to the rest of the body through the aorta.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pulmonary Circulation:**

 
 
• Pulmonary circulation is the movement of blood between the heart and the lungs.
 
• It involves the right ventricle pumping deoxygenated blood to the lungs via the pulmonary arteries.
 
• Oxygenated blood returns to the left atrium through the pulmonary veins.
 
 
 
• **Systemic Circulation:**
 
 
• Systemic circulation moves oxygenated blood from the heart to the rest of the body.
 
• The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta, which branches into smaller arteries and reaches tissues throughout the body.
 
 
 
• **Heart Chambers:**
 
 
• The heart has four chambers: two atria (upper chambers) and two ventricles (lower chambers).
 
• The atria receive blood, while the ventricles pump blood out of the heart.
 
 
 
• **Valves of the Heart:**
 
 
• Heart valves ensure one-way blood flow through the heart chambers.
 
• Major valves include the mitral valve (between left atrium and ventricle) and the tricuspid valve (between right atrium and ventricle).
